beats.text: Dozens of services. Which one does the client call?
beats.say: In a microservices app, how does a client know which of the dozens of services to call?

beats.text: Every client must know every service.
beats.say: Every client has to know every service, handle login for each one, and keep up with every change.

beats.text: One front door: the API gateway.
beats.say: An A P I gateway is the single front door. Clients only talk to it, and it routes each request to the right service.
It looks at the request, like slash users or slash orders, and forwards it to the matching service.

beats.text: Auth, rate limits, and logging in one place.
beats.say: It also handles the shared work in one place: authentication, rate limiting, and logging. Bad requests never reach your services.

beats.text: One call in, many services behind it.
beats.say: It can even combine several responses into one, so the client makes just a single call.
